title: Antigonus of Socho
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He is mentioned in Avot 1:3. He received the Torah from Shimon the Righteous, and there remains to us from him his precious saying: 'Do not be like servants who serve the master in order to receive a reward; rather, be like servants who serve the master not in order to receive a reward, and let the fear of Heaven be upon you.'

And in Avot de-Rabbi Natan, beginning of chapter 5: he had two students, one named Tzadok and the other named Baitos, who went astray because they erred in the words of their master: 'How is it possible that a laborer works all day and does not receive his wages in the evening?' And through this they denied the resurrection of the dead, and from them arose the sect called Sadducees and Boethusians. And see the entry Tzadok.
Yose ben Yoezer of Tzereidah and Yose ben Yochanan of Jerusalem received from Antigonus; and in Challah 4:11 it says that “Ben Antigonus” brought up firstborn animals from Babylonia and they did not accept from him. But there are other readings there.

notes.text: “Ben Antigonus” in the Challah quotation is a transmitted name; this notice does not establish that he was this Antigonus’s son.

The consulted Avot deRabbi Natan 5 describes repeated teaching through successive students and generations before the sect narrative; Hyman gives a compressed account of the two named disciples. The consulted Challah 4:11 witness reads Ben Antinos, where Hyman gives Ben Antigonus. Neither form establishes that this person was the son of the Antigonus in the heading.
